filmIssues: The pull-back idea is right for the scene, but the opening at zoom 1.38 is too tight: the scalloped archive border is cropped away and the woman holding the towel is awkwardly clipped at the left edge, so t=0 is not a good opening picture and the key figure intended for the reveal is already half lost.

The movement is only a modest centred pull-back; the swimmer is too small at the start for the tight opening to read as 'on the small swimmer', so it reads little better than a plain push-in in reverse.

cut-2 is only the towel, but the woman holding it remains in the background plate. Giving the towel depth 0.9 makes it parallax separately from her arm/body and risks a visible slide/doubled edge against her silhouette as the camera pulls back.
cut-1 swimmer scale 0.92 with driftY -0.02 lifts and shrinks him away from his painted ripples/reflection, risking a ghost/halo in the water and reading as sinking rather than swimming deeper.

rounds.verdict: Coherent, attractive pull-back, but too close to a plain zoom-out to publish as a story-led film; start tighter on the swimmer and make the pull-back a clearer reveal of Auntie Yolly and the full plate.
filmIssues: The pull-back is coherent and legible, but it is only a modest centred zoom-out (1.26 to 1.0) with very little pan or parallax between the contact-sheet frames; it reads as only slightly more expressive than a plain push-in played in reverse.

The intended story — a lone 5am swimmer gradually revealed within the wider pool, hills, steam and waiting Auntie Yolly — is present mainly in the final full-plate reveal, not in a strong opening composition. The first frame is already close to the whole scene, so the reveal feels timid.

No obvious tearing, doubled edges, halo or ghosting is visible on the swimmer or towel, and neither layer clips awkwardly, but the towel layer barely separates in depth from the woman/background, so the 2.5D move adds little depth.
The last frame is a good dwell image — the full scalloped archive plate — and the haze is fitting and subtle for steam at dawn, preserving the risograph print look.

plan.rationale: A clearer 5am pull-back that still works in reverse: open closer on the steaming pool and swimmer, but at 1.26 with focus pulled left/down so the waiting woman and full orange towel stay inside the frame alongside him and a hint of the scalloped border remains. Pull steadily back through 1.12 to the full plate at 1.0, revealing the border, hills, steam and waiting figure for the dwell frame. Keep

rounds.verdict: Do not publish as-is: a well-kept but timid pull-back whose opening and closing pictures are almost identical, so the 5am reveal never happens.
filmIssues: The intended pull-back reveal barely reads: all six frames show essentially the same full plate with the scalloped border intact, so t=0 is not a tight opening on the swimmer and t=1 is not a distinct reveal of the waiting woman.
The movement is no more expressive than a plain centred zoom - the swimmer, pool edge, hills and orange towel are all visible from the first frame, so the 5am entrance/reveal story is not told.
Haze is fitting for steam at dawn and stays subtle, and no tearing, doubled edges or ghosting is visible; the towel (cut-2) does stay registered on the woman's silhouette throughout.
The final frame is a good dwell picture (full pool, swimmer, woman and towel), but because the opening frame is nearly identical it earns no reveal in either direction.

plan.rationale: Make the 5am story a true reveal: open tighter at 1.40 on the steaming water and small swimmer seen from behind, with the focus low on the pool so he dominates the opening frame, then pull back steadily through 1.18 to the full plate at 1.0 while easing the pan left/up. The widening view progressively reveals the pool edge, hills and steam, and finally the waiting woman with the full orange towel
